knowledge:
- key_parameters: ncomp=number of independent components to extract ;; ntry=number of consensus runs to perform for stability ;; ncores=number of CPU cores for parallel processing ;; show.every=frequency of printing logs during consensus runs ;; filter.thr=threshold to filter out genes with low values ;; alpha=significance threshold for feature extraction and GO enrichment ;; db=Gene Ontology database categories to search ("BP", "MF", "CC") ;; icomp=index of the independent component to analyze ;; mode=plotting mode for ANOVA (e.g., 'box')
- alternatives: The documentation mentions DecompPipeline, MeDeCom, and FactorViz as alternative reference-free deconvolution methods for DNA methylation data.
- when_to_use: Use when deconvolving bulk or single-cell transcriptomics data to separate biological signals (cell types, pathways) from technical biases, perform feature engineering for patient classification, or link components to clinical metadata and survival.
- pitfalls: GO enrichment analysis (getGO) can be computationally slow, so parallelization (ncores) is recommended. Components may capture technical biases or gender differences (e.g., IC1 isolating gender), which should be identified via anovaIC and can be removed by reconstructing the expression matrix with zero weights for those components. Older package versions (< 1.1.1) required manual orientation adjustment via setOrientation when loading external GO objects.

workflows.name: consensus_ica_workflow
workflows.intent: Deconvolve transcriptomics data using consensus ICA, extract key features, associate components with clinical metadata and survival, perform GO enrichment, and generate an automated report.
input: samples_data (SummarizedExperiment object containing the gene expression matrix and sample metadata)
Sur (data.frame containing "time" and "event" columns for survival analysis)
workflows.stages: 1. Load data and extract expression, metadata, and survival variables ;; 2. Run consensus ICA deconvolution using consICA ;; 3. Extract top contributing features (genes) for components using getFeatures ;; 4. Estimate and plot variance explained using estimateVarianceExplained and plotICVarianceExplained ;; 5. Associate components with experimental factors using ANOVA via anovaIC ;; 6. Perform Gene Ontology enrichment analysis using getGO ;; 7. Perform survival analysis and calculate risk scores using survivalAnalysis ;; 8. Generate an automated PDF report using saveReport
workflows.code:
library('consICA')
library(SummarizedExperiment)
data("samples_data")
X <- data.frame(assay(samples_data))
Var <- data.frame(colData(samples_data))
Sur <- data.frame(colData(samples_data))[,c("time", "event")]
Var <- Var[,which(colnames(Var) != "time" & colnames(Var) != "event")]
set.seed(2022)
cica <- consICA(samples_data, ncomp=20, ntry=10, ncores=1, show.every=0)
features <- getFeatures(cica, alpha = 0.05, sort = TRUE)
head(features$ic.1$pos)
head(features$ic.1$neg)
icomp <- 1
plot(sort(cica$S[,icomp]),col = "#0000FF", type="l", ylab=("involvement"),xlab="genes",las=2,cex.axis=0.4, main=paste0("Metagene #", icomp, "\n(involvement of features)"),cex.main=0.6)
var_ic <- estimateVarianceExplained(cica)
p <- plotICVarianceExplained(cica)
var_ic1 <- anovaIC(cica, Var, icomp = 1, color_by_pv = TRUE, plot = TRUE)
var_ic5 <- anovaIC(cica, Var, icomp = 5, mode = 'box', plot = FALSE)
# cica <- getGO(cica, alpha = 0.05, db = "BP", ncores = 4)
# cica <- getGO(cica, alpha = 0.05, db = c("BP", "MF", "CC"), ncores = 4)
RS <- survivalAnalysis(cica, surv = Sur)
